title: China-Japan rare earth dispute
summary: A diplomatic dispute between China and Japan coincided with rare earth export disruption concerns, highlighting concentration risk in critical minerals used by electronics, autos, defense systems, and clean-energy equipment.
evidenceSnippets: China's rare earth export restrictions became a trade dispute with the United States, European Union, and Japan, and the 2010 episode increased investment in rare earth developments outside China.
Rare earth metals are used in magnets, defense products, electronics, and other advanced industrial applications.

title: China-related semiconductor export-control escalation
summary: U.S. and Chinese export-control actions tightened restrictions around advanced chips, semiconductor equipment, high-bandwidth memory, and critical chipmaking materials such as gallium, germanium, graphite, and antimony.
evidenceSnippets: U.S. measures restricted China's access to advanced semiconductor equipment, software, and high-bandwidth memory.
China responded with controls on critical chipmaking materials including gallium, germanium, antimony, and graphite.

title: COVID supply-chain shock
summary: COVID restrictions, labor disruptions, shipping bottlenecks, and demand swings created global supply-chain stress affecting retail inventories, electronics, autos, logistics, and inflation.
evidenceSnippets: The COVID pandemic and later disruptions slowed global supply chains and contributed to shortages across many product categories.
Ports, factories, and logistics networks faced backlogs as demand patterns shifted.

title: Global semiconductor shortage
summary: Pandemic demand shifts, capacity constraints, and auto/electronics supply-chain mismatches produced a semiconductor shortage that disrupted vehicle production, consumer electronics, cloud hardware, and industrial equipment.
evidenceSnippets: The U.S. response included a supply-chain review covering semiconductor chips, batteries, rare minerals, and pharmaceuticals.
Automakers and electronics companies faced production disruption as chip demand and available supply diverged.

title: Japan earthquake supply-chain disruption
summary: The Tohoku earthquake and tsunami disrupted Japanese industrial production and exposed global dependence on concentrated suppliers for autos, electronics, components, and semiconductor materials.
evidenceSnippets: The earthquake and tsunami caused severe infrastructure and production disruption in Japan.
Global manufacturers monitored component availability because Japanese suppliers were deeply embedded in electronics and automotive supply chains.

title: Oil price shock affecting airlines and energy producers
summary: The 2008 oil price spike sharply increased fuel costs for airlines and transportation while improving near-term earnings sensitivity for energy producers before demand destruction took hold.
evidenceSnippets: Crude oil prices rose sharply during the 2000s energy crisis, pressuring fuel-intensive transportation businesses.
Higher realized prices created positive earnings sensitivity for upstream energy producers before macro demand weakened.

title: U.S. regional banking crisis
summary: Silicon Valley Bank, Signature Bank, and First Republic failures created regional-bank contagion risk tied to uninsured deposits, duration losses, liquidity stress, and depositor concentration.
evidenceSnippets: In March 2023, several small-to-mid-sized U.S. banks failed and regulators intervened to reduce contagion risk.
Silicon Valley Bank's failure was tied to a bank run, unrealized securities losses, and a concentrated depositor base.

title: Russia-Europe energy shock
summary: Russia's invasion of Ukraine and subsequent gas dispute with Europe triggered energy-security stress, gas-price volatility, LNG competition, and margin pressure for energy-intensive European industries.
evidenceSnippets: The Russia-EU gas dispute flared after the February 2022 invasion of Ukraine and centered on natural gas pipeline flows to Europe.
Europe rapidly sought alternate gas supplies and reduced dependence on Russian fossil fuels.
